problem_text: Let p, q, r be three distinct prime numbers, t a positive integer. Let G be a finite group, H a normal subgroup of G such that |G/H| = r^t. Suppose H has a composition series {e} = H_0 ◁ H_1 ◁ H_2 = H with n=2, H_1/H_0 ≅ Z/pZ, H_2/H_1 ≅ Z/qZ. Further suppose G has a composition series {e} = G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ... ◁ G_n = G and positive integers i < j ≤ n such that G_i/G_{i-1} ≅ Z/qZ, G_j/G_{j-1} ≅ Z/pZ. Show that there exists a composition series of H with n=2, H_1/H_0 ≅ Z/qZ, H_2/H_1 ≅ Z/pZ.
solution_text: Proof sketch: |H| = pq since H has a composition series of length 2 with factors Z/pZ and Z/qZ. |G| = pq·r^t. Consider the subnormal series {e} ◁ H ◁ G and the given composition series of G. By the Schreier refinement theorem, both series have equivalent refinements. Refining {e} ◁ H ◁ G yields a composition series of G that restricts to a composition series of H (from refining {e} ◁ H) plus t copies of Z/rZ (from refining H ◁ G, since |G/H| = r^t). By the Zassenhaus lemma (butterfly lemma), the composition factors of H derived from G's composition series correspond to the non-r factors of G's series, namely Z/pZ and Z/qZ. Crucially, since r is distinct from both p and q, all r-factors belong to G/H and do not appear in H's derived series. Since Z/qZ appears at position i < j (position of Z/pZ) in G's composition series, the induced composition series of H has Z/qZ before Z/pZ. This gives a composition series of H of length 2 with factors [Z/qZ, Z/pZ], as required.
solution_summary: Use Schreier refinement theorem and Zassenhaus lemma to derive H's composition series from G's, preserving factor ordering. The distinctness of r from p,q ensures r-factors belong to G/H, so only Z/qZ and Z/pZ appear in H's series, with Z/qZ first (matching G's ordering).
answer: There exists a composition series of H with n=2, H_1/H_0 ≅ Z/qZ, H_2/H_1 ≅ Z/pZ (i.e., the composition factors of H can be reordered to have Z/qZ first and Z/pZ second).

rounds.question: List all theorems that relate the composition series of a group and its normal subgroup — which ones can transfer ordering information from G to H?
rounds.expected_answer: Relevant theorems: (1) Jordan-Hölder theorem — composition factors are unique up to permutation, (2) Schreier refinement theorem — any two subnormal series have equivalent refinements, (3) Zassenhaus lemma (butterfly lemma) — relates quotients of intersected subgroups, (4) Sylow theorems — for direct analysis of H's subgroup structure, (5) Correspondence theorem — relates subgroups of G/H to subgroups of G containing H. Schreier refinement and Zassenhaus are the key tools for transferring ordering information from G's series to H's series.

rounds.question: Try using Sylow theorems on H directly to show a normal subgroup of order q exists. What happens when p > q and p ≡ 1 mod q?
rounds.expected_answer: If p < q: n_q | p and n_q ≡ 1 mod q, since p < q we get n_q = 1, so Sylow q-subgroup is normal — done. If p > q: n_q | p and n_q ≡ 1 mod q, n_q could be 1 or p (if p ≡ 1 mod q). When p ≡ 1 mod q, the non-abelian group of order pq exists where Sylow q-subgroup is not normal. In this case Sylow alone cannot prove the existence of a normal subgroup of order q. The direct approach fails — we need to use G's composition series information.

rounds.question: Apply the Schreier refinement theorem to the subnormal series {e} ◁ H ◁ G and G's composition series — what does the refinement produce?
rounds.expected_answer: By Schreier refinement, the subnormal series {e} ◁ H ◁ G and G's composition series {e} = G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ... ◁ G_n = G have equivalent refinements. Refining {e} ◁ H ◁ G: the part {e} ◁ H refines to a composition series of H (factors Z/pZ and Z/qZ in some order), and H ◁ G refines to t copies of Z/rZ (since |G/H| = r^t). The refinement of G's composition series is itself (it's already a composition series). The two refinements are equivalent, meaning their composition factors match up to permutation.

rounds.question: Use the Zassenhaus lemma (butterfly lemma) to track which composition factors of G contribute to H's composition series. Why do the r-factors not appear in H's series?
rounds.expected_answer: By the Zassenhaus lemma, when we intersect G's composition series with H, the factors G_k/G_{k-1} where G_k ∩ H ≠ G_{k-1} ∩ H contribute to H's composition series. The r-factors (Z/rZ quotients) correspond to the G/H part — since |G/H| = r^t and r is distinct from p and q, these factors do not contribute to H (intersecting with H gives trivial quotients). Only the Z/pZ and Z/qZ factors contribute to H. Since Z/qZ appears at position i < j (position of Z/pZ) in G's series, the induced composition series of H has Z/qZ before Z/pZ.

The r-factors are excluded because they belong to G/H (|G/H| = r^t, r ≠ p,q). The Z/qZ factor from position i in G's series induces a factor in H's series before the Z/pZ factor from position j > i. So H's derived composition series is {e} ◁ K_1 ◁ H where K_1 has order q and H/K_1 ≅ Z/pZ, giving factors [Z/qZ, Z/pZ] of length 2.

rounds.question: Assemble the complete proof: Schreier refinement + Zassenhaus + factor ordering gives the desired composition series of H with factors [Z/qZ, Z/pZ].
rounds.expected_answer: Complete proof: (1) |H| = pq from the given composition series. (2) Consider subnormal series {e} ◁ H ◁ G and G's composition series. (3) By Schreier refinement, both have equivalent refinements. (4) By Zassenhaus lemma, intersecting G's series with H yields a composition series of H whose factors are the non-r factors of G's series. (5) Since r ≠ p,q, all r-factors belong to G/H, leaving only Z/pZ and Z/qZ for H. (6) Since Z/qZ appears at position i < j (Z/pZ) in G's series, H's derived series has Z/qZ before Z/pZ. (7) This gives a composition series of H of length 2 with factors [Z/qZ, Z/pZ]. QED.
